524.name: hep_whole_life_module
524.title: DISC Parent
524.description:
Safety Interventions Instructions for HEP

As a safety precaution, all participants who endorse current depression on the DISC must be referred for psychiatric evaluation. Please plan ahead for this possibility by creating a list of local mental health providers to be given to participants if needed.

Participants who are found to have a lifetime history of major depression on the DISC (MDD section) and who answer question 14 as their current age will be referred for psychiatric treatment.

With all psychiatric referrals, the phenotyping clinician should explain to the participant that the interview suggests that they should seek evaluation by a mental health provider; please emphasize that this is not a clinical diagnosis. The participant’s parent or guardian must also be notified immediately of any psychiatric diagnoses, including if the parent/guardian is not present during the C-SSRS administration. Lastly, please also ask for written permission from the participant and/or parent or guardian to contact their primary care provider and notify them of the participant’s DISC score indicative of depression.

After completion of the study visit:
- fill out the HEP Safety Intervention Form in REDCap, and
- follow up with the participant 1 week after referral to confirm they were able to schedule an appointment with a mental health provider.

If you have any questions or concerns as to a participant’s diagnosis, please contact Dr. Andres Kanner at 847-476-1811 (or if Dr. Kanner is unavailable, Dr. Siddhartha Nadkarni at 917-763-1016).

To be administered to parents of children ages seven and older for those diagnoses not present or “subthreshold” in current state.

Note: “Subthreshold” means that impairment and onset questions for the diagnosis were asked.

1.3.field_title: 1. Since [he/she] turned five years old, has there ever been a period of time when [he/she] seemed to worry too much about a number of different things … maybe things like whether [he/she] would make good grades in school … or how [he/she] would do in sports … or that [he/she] might have some sickness or illness?

1.4.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.5.field_title: 1A. Did [his/her] worrying too much about things go on for a long time, at least for several months in a row?

1.6.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.7.field_title: 1B. Did it seem like it was very hard for [him/her] to stop [himself/ herself] from worrying about these things?

1.8.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.9.field_title: 2. How old was [he/she] when [he/she] first started to worry so much? (Years)

1.12.field_title: 3. How old was [he/she] when [he/she] stopped worrying that much? (Years)

1.15.field_title: 4. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time [he/she] worried so much [between the ages of ___ and ___ /when [he/she] was ___ /when [he/she] was in ___ grade(s)].

1.16.field_title: Did it seem like worrying so much made it hard for [him/her] to keep [his/her] mind on other things?

1.18.field_title: 5. When [he/she] seemed worried like that, did [he/she] also seem tense, restless, or tired out?

1.20.field_title: 6. When [he/she] seemed worried like that, was [he/she] grouchy or irritable a lot of the time?

1.21.field_title: 7. Did worrying so much interfere with [his/her] sleep?

1.22.field_title: 8. Did it seem like worrying like that gave [him/her] headaches or other aches and pains?

1.23.field_title: 9. Did worrying like that seem to make [him/her] get tired very easily?

1.24.field_title: 10. Did worrying so much cause any serious problems for [him/her] at home, (at school) or with [his/her] friends?

1.25.field_title: 11. Did [he/she] ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that because [he/she] worried too much?

1.26.field_title: 12. Did worrying a lot seem to make [him/her] feel really unhappy or bother [him/her] a lot?

1.28.field_title: 1. Since [he/she] turned five years old, was there a time when [he/she] seemed nervous or uncomfortable almost every time [he/she] had to talk to people [he/she] didn’t know well?

1.29.field_title: 2. Since [he/she] turned five years old, was there a time when [he/she] seemed very nervous or uncomfortable almost every time [he/she] had to do something when other people were looking at [him/her] … like speaking in front of the class … or eating where other people could see [him/her] – like in the school lunchroom or at a restaurant?

1.30.field_title: IF ANY * RESPONSES WAS CODED IN Q 1 - 2, CONTINUE ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.31.field_title: 3. Now I want you to think about the reason [he/she] felt nervous or uncomfortable about [talking to people [he/she] didn’t know well/doing something when other people were looking at [him/her]]. Do you think this was because [he/she] was afraid that [he/she] would embarrass [himself/herself] or make a fool of [himself/herself]?

1.32.field_title: 4. Did [his/her] being nervous or uncomfortable whenever [he/she] [talked to people [he/she] didn’t know well/did something when other people were looking at [him/ her]] last several months in a row?

1.33.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.34.field_title: 5. How old was [he/she] when [he/she] first started being afraid of [talking to people [he/she] didn’t know well/doing something when other people were looking at [him/her]]?

1.37.field_title: 6. How old was [he/she] when [he/she] last was afraid of [talking to people [he/she] didn’t know well/doing something when other people were looking at [him/her]]?

1.40.field_title: 7. Now I want to ask you some questions about other things that were going on [between the ages of ___ and ___ /when [he/she] was ___ /when [he/she] was in ___ grade(s)]. During that time, did [he/she] have friends [his/her] age who [he/she] liked spending time with?

1.41.field_title: 8. Did being nervous or uncomfortable when [he/she] [talked to people [he/she] didn’t know well/did something when other people were looking at [him/her]] cause any serious problems for [him/her] at home, (at school) or with [his/her] friends?

1.42.field_title: 9. Did [he/she] ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that because [he/she] was nervous or uncomfortable when [he/she] [talked to people [he/she] didn’t know well/did something when other people were looking at [him/her]]?

1.43.field_title: 10. Did being nervous or uncomfortable when [he/she] [talked to people [he/she] didn’t know well/did something when other people were looking at [him/her]] seem to make [him/her] feel really unhappy or bother [him/her] a lot?

1.45.field_title: Since  [he/she] turned five years old, has there been a time when [he/she] was almost always very, very afraid of:

1.46.field_title: 1. Dogs, birds, snakes, insects, or any other animals?

1.47.field_title: 2. How about being really afraid of being up high or in a high place?

1.48.field_title: 3. How about being really afraid of thunder and lightening?

1.49.field_title: 4. … or being afraid of the dark?

1.50.field_title: 5. Was [he/she] very afraid of water, like a pool or a lake?

1.51.field_title: 6. … or being on a bridge … or in a tunnel … or on a highway?

1.52.field_title: 7. Was [he/she] really afraid of elevators or escalators?

1.53.field_title: 8. Was [he/she] very afraid of needles or shots?

1.54.field_title: 9. Was [he/she] really afraid to see blood or to see someone with a bad cut?

1.55.field_title: IF A YES RESPONSE WAS CODED IN Q 1 - 9, CONTINUE ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.56.field_title: 10. You said [he/she] was afraid of [NAME SPECIFIC FEAR(S)]. Was [he/she] afraid of [[NAME SPECIFIC FEAR]/any of those things] for several months in a row or longer?

1.57.field_title: IF MORE THAN ONE FEAR, ASK Q 10A, ALL OTHERS, GO TO Q 11

1.58.field_title: 10A. Which one(s) was [he/she] afraid of for several months or longer?

1.59.field_title: 11. How old was [he/she] when [he/she] first started to be afraid of (any of) [NAME FEAR(S)]?

1.62.field_title: 12. How old was [he/she] when [he/she] became less afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)]?

1.65.field_title: 13. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time [he/she] was afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)] [between ages ___ and ___ /when [he/she] was ___ /when [he/she] was in ___ grade(s)].  When [he/she]	had to [go in/go near/see/get/go on] [NAME FEAR(S)], did [it/ they] nearly always make [him/her] feel really upset?

1.66.field_title: 14. Was [he/she] so afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)] that [he/she] tried to stay away from [them/it]?

1.67.field_title: 14A. If [he/she] couldn’t stay away from [them/it], did [he/she] feel afraid the whole time [he/she] was there?

1.68.field_title: IF A YES RESPONSE WAS CODED IN Q 14 OR Q 14A, CONTINUE, ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.69.field_title: 15. Did being afraid like that cause any big problems for [him/her] at home, (at school) or with [his/her] friends?

1.70.field_title: 16. Did [he/she] ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that because [he/she] was afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)]?

1.71.field_title: 17. Did being afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)] make [him/her] feel really unhappy or bother [him/her] a lot?

1.73.field_title: 1. Since [he/she] turned five years old, was there ever a time when [he/she] had a sudden attack of feeling very scared and strange things would happen to [him/her], all at once … things like [he/she] couldn’t catch [his/her] breath … or [he/she] felt like [he/she] was choking … or [his/her] heart started beating really fast … or [his/her] chest hurt … or [he/she] felt dizzy … or [he/she] felt very hot or cold … or [he/she] felt like [he/she] was going to die or go crazy?

1.74.field_title: 1A. Would [he/she] have two or more of these feelings at the same time?

1.75.field_title: 1B. Did [he/she] say that several of these feelings started within the same few minutes, like an attack?

1.76.field_title: 1C. Has [he/she] had more than one attack like this?

1.77.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.78.field_title: 1D. Did these attacks ever come on when [he/she] didn’t expect them?

1.79.field_title: 2. How old was [he/she] when [he/she] first had one of these attacks?

1.82.field_title: 3. How old was [he/she] the last time [he/she] had one of these attacks?

1.85.field_title: 4. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time [he/she] was having these attacks [between the ages of ___ and ___ /when [he/she] was ___ /when [he/she] was in ___ grade(s)].  After [he/she] had an attack, did [he/she] seem to worry a lot that it might happen again?

1.86.field_title: 4A. Did [he/she] say that [he/she] worried that having these attacks meant there was something really wrong with [him/her]?

1.87.field_title: 4B. Did [he/she] stop doing things [he/she] liked because [he/she] thought [he/she] might have an attack if [he/she] did them?

1.88.field_title: 4C. Did [he/she] stop going places where [he/ she] might not be able to get help if [he/ she] had an attack?

1.89.field_title: 5. Did having these attacks cause any serious problems for [him/her] at home, (at school) or with [his/her] friends?

1.90.field_title: 6. Did [he/she] ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that about these attacks?

1.91.field_title: 7. Did having these attacks seem to make [him/her] feel really unhappy or bother [him/her] a lot?

1.93.field_title: 1. I’ll be asking you next about whether [he/she] has had a couple of weeks or more when [he/she] seemed depressed or sad most of the time or seemed like [he/she] didn’t enjoy things. I don’t mean just ordinary sadness; I mean a couple of weeks when nearly all the time [he/she] seemed really sad or miserable … or when [he/she] just couldn’t seem to enjoy anything as much as usual … or nothing [he/she] did seemed fun … or when [he/she] was so irritable or grouchy that everything got on [his/her] nerves. Since [he/she] turned five years old, has it ever seemed like [he/she] felt like that almost every day for a couple of weeks in a row?

1.94.field_title: 2. Which of the feelings I mentioned did [he/she] have at that time? That is, did [he/ she] seem sad all day long?

1.95.field_title: 3. Did it seem like [he/she] couldn’t enjoy anything or that nothing seemed fun?

1.96.field_title: 4. Did [he/she] seem really grouchy or irritable almost every day?

1.97.field_title: NOTE 2:	WAS A YES RESPONSE CODED IN Q 2 OR Q 4?

1.98.field_title: IF A YES RESPONSE WAS CODED IN Q 2 - 4, CONTINUE AND USE FIRST YES “MOOD” AS KEYWORD IN Q 5 - 20. ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.99.field_title: 5. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time [he/she] was [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable]. When [he/she] was [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], did it seem like it was hard for [him/her] to keep [his/her] mind on what [he/she] was doing, to think clearly, or to make up [his/her] mind about even little things?

1.100.field_title: 6. When [he/she] was [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], did [he/she] feel that [he/she] was “no good,” or did [he/she] blame [himself/herself] for all sorts of things?

1.101.field_title: 7. When [he/she] was [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], did [his/her] eating change … for example, did [he/she] eat much less than usual … or did [he/ she] eat a whole lot more than usual?

1.102.field_title: 8. Did [he/she] seem really tired all the time, or did it seem like [he/she] had so little energy that it took a big effort to do anything?

1.103.field_title: IF 5 OR MORE YES RESPONSES WERE CODED IN Q 3 - 8 AND NOTE 2, GO TO Q 13

1.104.field_title: 9. When [he/she] was [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], did [his/her] sleeping change so that [he/she] wanted to sleep all the time, or so that [he/she] had trouble with falling asleep or staying asleep?

1.129.field_title: 1. Now I want to ask about a time when you or other people were worried about [him/her] because [he/she] was getting too excited or happy, so excited or happy that nothing could calm [him/her] down. I don’t mean just being happy or excited because something really special was happening. I am talking about a real change from how [he/she] usually is, when there was nothing special going on … a change that lasted for several days, and made other people worry about [him/her]. Since [he/she] turned five years old, has [he/she] ever had a time like that?

1.130.field_title: 1A. Was there at least a whole week when [he/she] felt too happy or excited almost all the time?

1.131.field_title: 1B. Did [he/she] have to go to the hospital because you or other people were worried about the way [he/she] was acting?
